# PR #3117 Linux JIT attribution — predeclared diagnostic

This local diagnostic investigates managed JIT activity that persists during the hosted synchronous-batch workload. It does not establish performance acceptance, explain the hosted maximum-latency loss by itself, or authorize any tradeoff.

Use the retained Linux Loaded-A and Loaded-B binaries from run 34176568856, without rebuilding them. Producer remains A (5df2f0d03607389384b5c1466e17812a9084fac9); consumer remains B (2a550007ccb091e8f2bf9275a7646277e984dff8); the fixture is measurement harness 7614406221b63c0b758f25e0722c8a3bf3ef9d0f. Main subsequently advanced to tooling-only 9eec358dad2a081dedbbfc75f02aee743e6bdad9. These old exact pins are retained for attribution, not fresh-main acceptance.

Run one traced smoke fixture (2 seconds warmup, 2 seconds measured, 1,000 records/s) to verify the container, trace capture, clock/PID correlation and workload correctness. This smoke is not performance evidence. If it fails, diagnose before timing.

Then run three fresh, sequential consumer processes: U1 untraced, T traced, U2 untraced. Each uses a fresh Kafka 4.3.1 broker and topic; 121 seconds of offered warmup and 120 seconds measured at 50,000 records/s. Keep four partitions, 256-byte payloads, capacity 128, concurrency 2, 1,024 keys, synchronous batch handler and maximum batch size 16 unchanged. Validate at least 120 seconds of actual handler warmup, exact completion/acknowledgement/commit counts, no failures or final backlog/pending handlers, raw latency accounting and actual batch sizes. Retain every warmup and measured sample and maximum.

Use the existing Linux SDK image sha256:e1ffd2a92ae84c1291bc1b6887501f8af98e6331e7af6d4c8d37168c5e87a64c and Kafka image sha256:77e3df9054047a88b520d0cc46e16696d3b22022e1d580aeccd2632df6532837. Record actual SDK/runtime and CPU topology before timing. Workstation GC, DOTNET_TieredCompilation=1 and DOTNET_GCDynamicAdaptationMode=0 match the hosted loaded workload. Pin broker to CPU 0, producer to CPU 1, consumer to CPUs 2/3; reserve CPU 4 for the collector. The local Docker VM has 20 logical CPUs and differs from GitHub hardware. All phases use the same assignments; the extra collector CPU is a diagnostic adaptation.

The traced process uses retained dotnet-trace 9.0.652701 under the installed .NET 10 runtime with an explicit tool-only --roll-forward Major launch argument. Enable only Microsoft-Windows-DotNETRuntime:0x10:5, a 128 MB buffer, no rundown and a seven-minute cap. Launch tracing before workload start, using a wrapper that records the exact consumer PID and then execs dotnet. This is JIT attribution, not native/kernel wait-time analysis. Capture method names, signatures, IDs, tiers, PIDs and raw QPC timestamps with the retained AdminJitTraceInspector. Require zero lost trace events and coverage spanning the measured boundaries; verify clock scale and PID before correlating events.

Report U1/T/U2 absolute completed throughput, actual message p50/p99/max, consumer CPU and allocations/message, JIT count/time, thread-pool/GC/heap/RSS/backlog trends and trace overhead/differences. Quarter-window or event-neighborhood diagnostics must not replace the full measurements. The existing 3% throughput/CPU, 5% latency and 1 B/message allocation thresholds provide context only; local diagnostics cannot produce PASS. Differences between U1 and U2 quantify this sample's drift; the traced run is not a product optimization. Do not average away drift or infer causation solely from nearby events.

Stop after these three measured processes. No automatic extra identical run or full paid campaign follows. Preserve all original logs, outputs, trace, parser, generated orchestration scripts and exact loaded inputs outside removable worktrees before publishing. Stop/remove only these named diagnostic containers and their own anonymous volumes.
